result.title: Asset4D-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Editable 3D and 4D Reconstruction
result.comment: The first three authors contributed equally
result.summary: A cart can follow its reference trajectory while its cargo floats above the deck. Asset4D-Bench tests whether coding agents recover objects, motion and interactions from visual references as editable Blender scenes. Its 114 conditions span image editing, video reconstruction with matched full or partial starter assets, and independently selected from-scratch tasks. We independently reopen projects and measure them against native reference states. The 228 archived scores include original delivery outcomes and versioned measures of scene quality. On 24 from-scratch tasks, each model earns full dynamics credit on 14. Of these, three GPT-6.1-Sol and eight GPT-6-Astra reconstructions earn zero relation points. Under the fixed scoring weights, relations contribute 5.15 points to the 6.50-point Sol-minus-Astra difference in mean recovered fidelity. Differences in execution and recovery policy across archived runs preclude a causal estimate of starter-asset effects.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Asset4D-Bench，要求 coding agents 从图像或视频参考重建可编辑的 Blender 3D/4D 场景，覆盖 114 个条件，并通过独立重开项目、按对象、动力学与交互关系分别计分来评测重建保真度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把重建拆为物体、运动与实体关系并独立复核、按版本计分的做法，可能为检验 LVR 内部状态是否保留几何细节与关系信息提供评价线索；但该工作是 3D 资产构建与打分而非 latent 推理，联系较远，需核查关系分项是否可迁移。
